name: Kettering Half Marathon & 5K
course: Undulating closed-road half through Kettering, Boughton House grounds and country lanes; shorter 5K route separate.
transport: Wicksteed Park, Barton Road; confirm race parking and arrival gate in the event guide.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and finish refreshments.
rules: Half minimum age 17; 5K minimum age 11; three-hour road-closure limit.
reason: The half combines town streets and countryside with 182m of climbing. Its three-hour limit should be checked before entering if you expect a steady pace.

name: Drayton Manor 5K & 10K
course: Flat tarmac route through the theme park: 5K one lap, 10K two laps.
transport: Free on-site parking; runners and spectators cannot leave by car until after 11:00.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets and 10K halfway water; no on-course water for 5K. Race entry includes park admission.
rules: Minimum age 15 for 10K, 11 for 5K. Spectators need a separate ticket; dogs are not allowed.
reason: Included theme-park admission adds value, but the enforced car exit time affects the rest of your day. Know that the 5K has no water station.

name: Leicestershire Half Marathon
course: Single-lap closed-road route via Shepshed, Belton and Hathern; undulating, mainly tarmac with some grass.
transport: Start is at Charnwood College, Thorpe Hill; use the final guide for parking and access.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village.
rules: Check footwear for grass sections and allow for an uneven effort on the hills.
reason: The single-loop countryside course avoids repeat laps, but mixed surface and rolling terrain may make road-race pacing harder.

name: Milton Keynes Festival of Running
course: Wide city roads at the start, then mostly flat routes; follow the map for your chosen distance.
transport: Event starts near Xscape, 602 Marlborough Gate; check city-centre parking and closures.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village.
rules: The four distances have different starts. Only the 20-mile route has a published 165m ascent on the organiser page.
reason: The 20-mile option fits marathon preparation four weeks before London, while the later half start changes travel planning.
